summary: This informational document describes KCipher-2, a stream cipher with a 128-bit key and a 128-bit initialization vector. Its algorithm was published in 2007 and has been evaluated in academic and industrial studies; no vulnerabilities had been found at the time. It is fast thanks to simple operations.

eli5.summary: This describes a secret-code machine that scrambles data quickly by making a long stream of mixed-up numbers.

questions: stream cipher based on shift registers
subtitle: A fast stream cipher algorithm using simple operations and multiple feedback shift registers

tldr.problem: Stream ciphers require fast, simple operations to be practical for resource-constrained environments, but must maintain strong cryptographic security against modern attacks.
tldr.mechanism: KCipher-2 uses two feedback shift registers (FSRs) with carefully chosen feedback polynomials, four internal registers, and substitution functions based on AES operations to generate a pseudo-random key stream that is XORed with plaintext.
tldr.outcome: Provides fast encryption in software and hardware with a 128-bit key and 128-bit IV, evaluated for security across academic and industrial studies with no successful attacks found.

facts.label: Operations used
facts.value: XOR, addition modulo 2^32, bit shift, table lookup

facts.label: Rekey recommendation
facts.value: After 2^58 cycles or 2^64 key stream bits

today: RFC 7008 documents KCipher-2 as an informational standard for reference and implementation. While it has proven secure in practice, modern deployments often prefer well-known standardized ciphers like AES-GCM for broader compatibility.

sections.title: Overview and Design
sections.content:
KCipher-2 is a stream cipher algorithm published in 2007 that accepts a 128-bit key and a 128-bit initialization vector (IV) to generate a key stream of arbitrary length. The algorithm uses only four simple operations: exclusive-OR, addition modulo 2^32, bit shifting, and table lookup. This simplicity allows efficient implementation in both software and hardware, making it suitable for embedded systems and mobile devices with limited computational resources. The internal state representation requires only several hundred bits, much smaller than modern block ciphers.

Since its publication, KCipher-2 has been rigorously evaluated by academic researchers and industry security experts, and as of the time this RFC was written, no vulnerabilities had been discovered. The algorithm has been adopted in Japanese industrial applications for mobile health monitoring and diagnostic services, and was designated as a recommended cipher by the Japanese e-Government organization. It was also standardized as part of ISO/IEC 18033-4.
sections.eli5: KCipher-2 is a fast secret-code machine that clever people have tested thoroughly and found to be safe. It works quickly on small computers.

sections.title: Internal State and Registers
sections.content:
The internal state of KCipher-2 consists of six components: Feedback Shift Register A (FSR-A), Feedback Shift Register B (FSR-B), and four internal registers (L1, R1, L2, R2). FSR-A is composed of five 32-bit units while FSR-B has eleven 32-bit units, for a total state size of about 512 bits. Each 32-bit unit stores values in the finite field GF(2^32). The two feedback shift registers are the primary state containers, while the four internal registers hold intermediate computation results.

The algorithm operates in cycles by applying a transformation function called next() to the state, which updates each register through non-linear substitutions and feedback functions. The feedback functions in the shift registers use carefully selected elements (a0, a1, a2, a3) that are roots of irreducible polynomials chosen to maximize the period of the generated key stream. These fixed elements were selected using finite field theory to guarantee that the feedback polynomials produce maximum-length sequences.
sections.eli5: Think of the state as five shuffling boxes and eleven bigger boxes holding numbers, plus four scratch pads. Each step mixes these boxes according to special math rules.

sections.title: Key Algorithm Operations
sections.content:
KCipher-2 defines three main operations: init(), next(), and stream(). The init() operation takes the 128-bit key and 128-bit IV as input and prepares the internal state for key stream generation. It first expands the key into a 384-bit internal key, then initializes all registers using both the expanded key and the IV. To maximize diffusion and security, it applies the next() operation in INIT mode twenty-four times, each application mixing the state further.

The next() operation transforms the current state into a new state by updating all registers. It applies substitution functions to internal registers and updates the feedback shift registers using the fixed feedback polynomials. When operating in NORMAL mode (during key stream generation), it updates FSRs without non-linear function output. When operating in INIT mode (during initialization), it also XORs the FSR updates with non-linear function outputs to further scramble the state.

The stream() operation extracts a 64-bit key stream value from the current state by applying non-linear functions to specific register values. To generate successive key stream blocks, the application calls next(state, NORMAL) followed by stream(state) repeatedly, advancing the state after each 64-bit output.
sections.eli5: Init prepares the boxes by mixing them 24 times with the secret key. Next shuffles the boxes according to the rules. Stream pulls out the scrambled numbers to mix with your message.

sections.title: Substitution and Mixing Functions
sections.content:
The algorithm incorporates a substitution function called sub_K2() that serves as a non-linear mixing operation. This function is based on components from the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). It takes a 32-bit input divided into four 8-bit bytes, applies the AES S-Box substitution table to each byte independently, and then applies a 32-bit linear permutation identical to the AES MixColumn operation. Using the existing AES S-Box simplifies implementation and leverages a well-studied cryptographic component.

A non-linear function (NLF) combines four 32-bit values using addition modulo 2^32 and exclusive-OR: the result is (A +32 B) XOR C XOR D. This simple operation provides non-linearity without complex arithmetic. Additionally, multiplications in the finite field GF(2^32) are pre-calculated into lookup tables (amul0, amul1, amul2, amul3) to accelerate the feedback polynomial computations. This trade-off of memory for speed is practical because the tables are small (4 KB total) and the speedup is significant.
sections.eli5: Substitution means swapping numbers according to a secret table. Mixing means combining values with XOR and addition. Using tables instead of calculations makes the cipher run faster.

sections.title: Message Encryption and Decryption
sections.content:
Encryption is performed by generating a key stream from the initialized state and XORing it with the plaintext message, a standard stream cipher technique. To encrypt, call init(key, IV) to create state S(0), call stream(S(0)) to get the first 64-bit key stream block X(0), and XOR each 64-bit plaintext block with the corresponding key stream block. To generate subsequent key stream blocks, repeatedly apply S(i+1) = next(S(i), NORMAL) and X(i+1) = stream(S(i+1)).

Decryption is identical to encryption: generate the same key stream from the same key and IV, and XOR the ciphertext with it to recover the plaintext. This is because XOR is its own inverse. The RFC recommends reinitializing and rekeying after 2^58 cycles (2^64 key stream bits generated), and emphasizes that no IV should ever be reused under the same key, as this would reveal the key stream and break security.
sections.eli5: Scrambling is mixing the message with the scrambled number stream. Unscrambling is doing the same thing again, since mixing twice gets you back to the start.

layers.label: Output: 32-bit result
layers.detail: Used as substituted value in state updates
